entries.note: “Mostly a nothing burger” judges the advance’s significance without specifying a factual threshold.

entries.test: OpenAI’s public release records would establish whether GPT-5 was available when the post was published.
entries.note: The context supports a claim that GPT-5 had not materialized publicly. “Does not exist” additionally rules out an unreleased model, which his words do not establish.
The physical-law assertion can be assessed separately. The combined claim leaves the set of prior statements and the meaning of “pretty much everything” unspecified.

entries.test: Public statements by Cowen and comparable AI influencers would show whether they blamed users, while their published expectations could be compared with GPT-4.5’s demonstrated results.
entries.note: This combines an undated prediction of public blame with an assessment of results against expectations. The forecast supplies no deadline.

entries.test: Contemporaneous investment estimates, financial disclosures, evidence of sustainable revenues and competitive barriers, and OpenAI’s release history would test the stated industry conditions at publication.
entries.note: “In AI” broadens a passage about generative AI and massive LLM scaling to the entire AI industry. The financial and competitive assertions nevertheless admit public evidence.

The imagined quotation expresses Marcus’s own endorsed assessment. The Apollo spending comparison is separately checkable, but “not that much to show for it” judges the return’s worth without a shared threshold.
